extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers; creative-writing students and instructors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing short stories and fiction focusing on the elements of narrative craft (from initial freewriting through revision) to produce exciting, fresh stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Work through problems in plot to create a coherent, compelling narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book addresses how writers must work through problems in plot (alongside other elements) to write exciting and fresh stories; treatment likely includes development, structure, pacing, and problem-solving across drafting and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and refine a distinctive prose style appropriate to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style is treated as a central element of fiction craft; writers are guided from initial drafting to revision to solve stylistic problems so the story reads freshly and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Create believable, alive characters whose desires and actions drive the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book discusses working through characterization problems during drafting and revision to ensure characters feel vivid and motivate plot choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Write authentic, purposeful dialogue that reveals character and advances the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue is presented as an element requiring revision and craft—balancing realism, subtext, and clarity so speech serves the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and sustain a sense of mood or atmosphere appropriate to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atmosphere (setting, tone, mood) is a named element to be shaped through imagery, diction, and scene construction across drafting and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete sensory detail and figurative language to create vivid images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imagery is emphasized as a tool for making writing fresh and exciting; guidance likely covers selection, restraint, and integration of image into narrative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and sustain an appropriate narrative point of view (voice, vantage) for the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point of view is treated as a craft decision affecting how readers experience events; the book discusses problems and solutions related to POV in drafting and revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing process: freewriting through revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a process that moves from freewriting and discovery to careful revision and problem-solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide 'ranges from freewriting to revision,' emphasizing that writers must work through problems in plot, style, characterization, etc., across multiple stages of writing to achieve strong fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excitement and freshness (originality/vitality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to write stories that feel exciting and fresh to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book's stated goal is helping writers produce 'exciting and fresh stories' by addressing and resolving problems in the various elements of fiction; examples and short stories are included to model this quality.
